spatial_claims.claim: ABCD is a circle with diameter BC and centre F; F lies on segment BC
A is on the circle, on the semicircle determined by diameter BC
BD is a chord not passing through the centre; A is on the major arc of BD
E is on the minor arc of BD
angle BAC = angle BAF + angle FAC; ray AF lies between rays AB and AC from vertex A
angle ABC = angle ABF and angle BCA = angle ACF because F lies on segment BC
B, F, C are collinear with F between B and C; angles BFA and AFC are supplementary (sum to 2R)
Central angle BFD = 2 times inscribed angle BAD, both subtending the minor arc BD not containing A
Minor arc BD is less than a semicircle, so central angle BFD < 2R and angle BAD < R
ABDE is a cyclic quadrilateral with vertices in order B, A, D, E around the circle; opposite angles BAD and BED sum to 2R
Angle of the greater segment (mixed angle between major arc and chord BD at B) exceeds the angle of the semicircle because the arc is larger
Angle of the less segment is contained within the angle of the semicircle and is therefore less than a right angle

configuration_map: Circle ABCD with center F and diameter BC. F is the midpoint of BC, lying on segment BC between B and C. Point A is on the circle, positioned on the semicircle on one side of diameter BC, and also on the major arc of chord BD. Point D is on the circle such that BD is a chord not passing through the center, with A on the major arc side. Point E is on the minor arc of BD, on the opposite side of chord BD from A. From vertex A, ray AF points toward F on segment BC, falling strictly between rays AB and AC (since F is between B and C on the diameter). Triangles ABF and AFC are isosceles (radii FB=FA and FC=FA). The cyclic quadrilateral BADE has vertices in order around the circle, with A and E on opposite arcs of chord BD.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The key angle decomposition (angle BAC = angle BAF + angle FAC) is valid because F lies on segment BC between B and C, placing ray AF between rays AB and AC from vertex A. The supplementary angle relation at F (angles BFA + AFC = 2R) is consistent with F being on line BC. The isosceles triangle properties, inscribed angle theorem (3.20), and cyclic quadrilateral theorem (3.22) are all applied with configurations matching the established positions of points. The mixed-angle arguments in Steps 16-19 are somewhat rambling in exposition but contain no contradictory spatial claims.
